assertion: Government data indicate that construction is short about 300,000 workers.
warehouse_value: econ.jolts_industry: construction (industry_code 230000) job openings level (JOL) = 326,000 in July 2026; 298,000 June 2026; 291,000 May 2026
sql: SELECT "year", "date", metric_type, value FROM econ.jolts_industry WHERE industry_code='230000' AND metric_type IN ('JOL','JOR') AND "year">=2025 ORDER BY "year" DESC, "date" DESC FETCH FIRST 30 ROWS ONLY
reason: Independently reproduced from BLS JOLTS via a live warehouse query; matches NAHB's rounded figure almost exactly. Caveat: JOLTS job openings is a proxy for shortage, not a direct shortage count.

assertion: Immigrant workers... account for more than one-quarter of the construction workforce [26.3%, a 2024 record high].
warehouse_value: census.acs_nativity: national foreign-born share of total population = 13.9% (46,108,901 / 332,387,540) in 2023, all industries combined; census.acs_industry has no nativity breakdown so the construction-specific 26.3% figure cannot be recomputed in this corpus
sql: SELECT SUM(total_population) AS total_pop, SUM(foreign_born) AS total_foreign_born FROM census.acs_nativity WHERE "year"='2023' AND geography='state'
independent_value: 26.3% (NAHB's own analysis of Census ACS microdata, authored by Natalia Siniavskaia), independently reported by multiple trade outlets
